Autodiff Integration Analysis for Powerful.jl

Current Architecture Summary

Gather-Compute-Scatter Pattern

The current residual evaluation follows this flow:

# 1. System-level (system.jl:454-477)
function evaluate_system_residuals!(sys_ws::SystemResidualWorkspace, dae::DAE)
    for (model_name, workspace) in pairs(sys_ws.model_workspaces)
        evaluate_model_residuals!(workspace, model_vec, dae, metadata)
    end
end

# 2. Model-level (system.jl:500-523)
function evaluate_model_residuals!(ws::ResidualWorkspace, model_vec, dae, metadata)
    gather_variables!(ws, dae)      # dae.y[addrs] → ws.var_vals
    calc_residuals!(ws, model_vec)  # compute ws.res_vals from ws.var_vals
    scatter_residuals!(ws, dae)     # ws.res_vals → dae.g[addrs]
end

# 3. Pure kernel (e.g., pq.jl:212-235)
@inline function pq_residual_kernel!(outputs, params, vars, active, ::Type{<:Vector})
    @inbounds @simd for i in eachindex(outputs.p)
        mask = active[i]
        vi = vars.v[i]
        outputs.p[i] = -mask * (params.pl[i] + params.ip[i] * vi + params.yp[i] * vi^2)
    end
end

Key Characteristics

  • Indirect addressing: Variables scattered across dae.y via var_addrs
  • Local buffers: ws.var_vals and ws.res_vals for gather-compute-scatter
  • Type-stable kernels: Pure computation with NamedTuples
  • CPU/GPU dispatch: Same interface for both backends

Julia Autodiff Requirements

Expected Function Signature

Julia autodiff tools expect a simple mutating function:

function residuals!(g::AbstractVector, y::AbstractVector)
    # Compute residuals: g .= f(y)
    # where g and y are flat vectors
end

Or non-mutating:

g = residuals(y::AbstractVector)

Sparse Jacobian Workflow

Two main approaches:

Approach 1: NonlinearSolve.jl (High-level)

using NonlinearSolve, SparseDiffTools

# Define problem with automatic sparsity detection
prob = NonlinearProblem(
    NonlinearFunction(residuals!;
                     sparsity = SymbolicsSparsityDetection()),
    y0
)

# Solve with sparse autodiff
sol = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson(autodiff = AutoSparseForwardDiff()))

Approach 2: Manual Sparse Jacobian (Low-level)

using SparseDiffTools, Symbolics, ForwardDiff

# Detect sparsity pattern (one-time setup)
sparsity_pattern = Symbolics.jacobian_sparsity(residuals!, g, y)
colorvec = SparseDiffTools.matrix_colors(sparsity_pattern)

# Pre-allocate sparse Jacobian
J = Float64.(sparsity_pattern)

# Compute Jacobian using coloring
forwarddiff_color_jacobian!(J, residuals!, y;
                           colorvec=colorvec,
                           sparsity=sparsity_pattern)

Integration Strategies

Strategy 1: Wrapper Function (Minimal Changes)

Pros: No changes to existing code, works immediately Cons: Less efficient (extra allocations), doesn't leverage existing workspaces

"""
Create a simple wrapper that calls the existing evaluate_system_residuals!
"""
function make_residual_function(sys::SystemModel, sys_ws::SystemResidualWorkspace)
    dae = DAE(Float64, sys)

    function residuals!(g::AbstractVector, y::AbstractVector)
        # Update DAE with current guess
        copyto!(dae.y, y)

        # Use existing infrastructure
        evaluate_system_residuals!(sys_ws, dae)

        # Extract residuals
        copyto!(g, dae.g)

        return nothing
    end

    return residuals!
end

# Usage
residuals! = make_residual_function(sys, sys_ws)

# Option 1: Use with NonlinearSolve.jl
using NonlinearSolve
prob = NonlinearProblem(
    NonlinearFunction(residuals!; sparsity=SymbolicsSparsityDetection()),
    dae.y
)
sol = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson(autodiff=AutoSparseForwardDiff()))

# Option 2: Manual Jacobian computation
using SparseDiffTools, Symbolics
g = similar(dae.y)
sparsity = Symbolics.jacobian_sparsity(residuals!, g, dae.y)
colors = SparseDiffTools.matrix_colors(sparsity)
J = Float64.(sparsity)
forwarddiff_color_jacobian!(J, residuals!, dae.y; colorvec=colors)

Strategy 2: Direct Jacobian Hooks (More Efficient)

Pros: Leverages existing workspace, no extra allocations, more control Cons: Requires adding new methods, more complex

Add a new method that computes Jacobian directly:

# In system.jl
"""
Evaluate both residuals and Jacobian using dual numbers for autodiff.
This allows autodiff tools to efficiently compute derivatives.
"""
function evaluate_system_residuals_dual!(
    sys_ws::SystemResidualWorkspace{T},
    dae::DAE{AT},
    y_dual::AbstractVector{<:ForwardDiff.Dual}
) where {T, AT}
    # Similar structure to evaluate_system_residuals!
    # but works with dual numbers

    # Create dual-number version of DAE
    dae_dual = DAE{typeof(y_dual)}(dae.m, similar(y_dual), y_dual)
    fill!(dae_dual.g, zero(eltype(y_dual)))

    for (model_name, workspace) in pairs(sys_ws.model_workspaces)
        model_vec = getfield(sys_ws.model_vectors, model_name)
        metadata = getfield(sys_ws.model_metadata, model_name)

        # This dispatches to dual-number aware versions
        evaluate_model_residuals_dual!(workspace, model_vec, dae_dual, metadata)
    end

    return dae_dual.g
end

Strategy 3: Symbolic Sparsity Declaration (Best for Large Systems)

Pros: Fastest, no symbolic tracing overhead after setup Cons: Requires manual sparsity pattern declaration

# In system.jl
"""
Declare the sparsity pattern of the Jacobian based on model connectivity.
This is much faster than symbolic detection for large systems.
"""
function jacobian_sparsity_pattern(sys::SystemModel)
    am = sys.address_manager
    n = length(dae.y)

    I = Int[]  # Row indices
    J = Int[]  # Column indices

    for (model_name, model_vec) in pairs(sys.models)
        base_type = get_base_model_type(model_vec)
        metadata = model_metadata(base_type)

        # For each residual, determine which variables it depends on
        for residual in metadata.residuals
            res_addrs = get_residual_addresses(am, model_name, residual.name)

            for var in metadata.vars
                var_addrs = get_variable_addresses(am, model_name, var.name)

                # Add dependency: residual depends on variable
                for r_addr in res_addrs
                    for v_addr in var_addrs
                        push!(I, r_addr)
                        push!(J, v_addr)
                    end
                end
            end
        end
    end

    # Create sparse pattern matrix
    return sparse(I, J, ones(Bool, length(I)), n, n)
end

Recommended Approach: Hybrid Strategy

Start with Strategy 1 (wrapper) for immediate functionality, then optimize:

# ==============================================================================
# NEW FILE: src/powercore/autodiff.jl
# ==============================================================================

module AutodiffInterface

using Powerful: SystemModel, SystemResidualWorkspace, DAE, evaluate_system_residuals!
using LinearAlgebra
using SparseArrays

export make_residual_function, jacobian_sparsity_pattern

"""
    make_residual_function(sys::SystemModel, T::Type=Float64)

Create a residual function compatible with Julia's autodiff ecosystem.

Returns a tuple `(residuals!, dae, sys_ws)` where:
- `residuals!(g, y)`: Mutating function for NonlinearSolve.jl
- `dae`: Pre-allocated DAE structure (contains initial guess)
- `sys_ws`: System workspace (keep alive to prevent GC)

# Example with NonlinearSolve.jl
\```julia
residuals!, dae, sys_ws = make_residual_function(sys)

using NonlinearSolve
prob = NonlinearProblem(
    NonlinearFunction(residuals!; sparsity=SymbolicsSparsityDetection()),
    copy(dae.y)  # Initial guess
)
sol = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson(autodiff=AutoSparseForwardDiff()))
\```

# Example with manual Jacobian
\```julia
residuals!, dae, sys_ws = make_residual_function(sys)

using SparseDiffTools, Symbolics
g = similar(dae.y)
sparsity = Symbolics.jacobian_sparsity(residuals!, g, dae.y)
colors = SparseDiffTools.matrix_colors(sparsity)
J = Float64.(sparsity)

# In Newton iteration
for iter in 1:max_iter
    forwarddiff_color_jacobian!(J, residuals!, dae.y; colorvec=colors)
    residuals!(g, dae.y)

    Δy = J \\ g
    dae.y .-= Δy

    if norm(g, Inf) < tol
        break
    end
end
\```
"""
function make_residual_function(sys::SystemModel, ::Type{T}=Float64) where T
    # Create workspace and DAE
    sys_ws = SystemResidualWorkspace(T, sys)
    dae = DAE(T, sys)

    # Create closure that captures workspace
    function residuals!(g::AbstractVector, y::AbstractVector)
        # Update DAE state
        copyto!(dae.y, y)

        # Evaluate using existing infrastructure
        evaluate_system_residuals!(sys_ws, dae)

        # Extract residuals
        copyto!(g, dae.g)

        return nothing
    end

    return residuals!, dae, sys_ws
end

"""
    jacobian_sparsity_pattern(sys::SystemModel)

Compute the sparsity pattern of the Jacobian ∂g/∂y based on model structure.

This is faster than symbolic detection for large systems and only needs to be
called once during setup.

Returns a `SparseMatrixCSC{Bool}` representing the Jacobian structure.

# Example
\```julia
# Get sparsity pattern
sparsity = jacobian_sparsity_pattern(sys)

# Use with SparseDiffTools
using SparseDiffTools
colors = matrix_colors(sparsity)
J = Float64.(sparsity)  # Pre-allocate Jacobian with correct sparsity

# In solver loop
residuals!, dae, sys_ws = make_residual_function(sys)
forwarddiff_color_jacobian!(J, residuals!, dae.y; colorvec=colors)
\```
"""
function jacobian_sparsity_pattern(sys::SystemModel)
    am = sys.address_manager

    # Determine size
    n = 0
    for (key, addrs) in am.addresses
        addr_type, _, _ = key
        if addr_type isa AlgebVar || addr_type isa AlgebRes
            if !isempty(addrs)
                n = max(n, maximum(addrs))
            end
        end
    end

    I = Int[]
    J = Int[]

    # Build sparsity pattern from model structure
    for (model_name, model_vec) in pairs(sys.models)
        if length(model_vec) == 0
            continue
        end

        base_type = get_base_model_type(model_vec)
        metadata = model_metadata(base_type)

        # Get all variable addresses for this model
        var_addr_lists = []
        for var in metadata.vars
            addrs = if is_internal(var)
                am.assignments[model_name].by_type[var.address_type][var.name]
            else
                am.retrieved[model_name].by_type[var.address_type][var.name]
            end
            push!(var_addr_lists, addrs)
        end

        # Get all residual addresses for this model
        for residual in metadata.residuals
            res_addrs = if is_internal(residual)
                am.assignments[model_name].by_type[residual.address_type][residual.name]
            else
                am.retrieved[model_name].by_type[residual.address_type][residual.name]
            end

            # Each residual depends on all variables of this model instance
            # (conservative estimate - could be refined per-model)
            for i in eachindex(res_addrs)
                r_addr = res_addrs[i]
                for var_addrs in var_addr_lists
                    v_addr = var_addrs[i]
                    push!(I, r_addr)
                    push!(J, v_addr)
                end
            end
        end
    end

    return sparse(I, J, ones(Bool, length(I)), n, n)
end

end  # module AutodiffInterface

Demo: Complete Example

# ==============================================================================
# NEW FILE: examples/autodiff_demo.jl
# ==============================================================================

using Powerful
using Powerful
using Powerful.Models
using PowerFlowData

# Load test case
case = PowerFlowData.parse_network(joinpath(pkgdir(Powerful), "cases", "ieee14.raw"))

# Parse models
bus = parse_model(Bus, case)
pq = parse_model(PQ, case)
pv = parse_model(PV, case)
branch = parse_model(Branch, case)

# Create system
am = AddressManager()
models = (; Bus=bus, PQ=pq, PV=pv, Branch=branch)
sys = SystemModel(am, models)

println("System size: $(length(sys)) models")

# ==============================================================================
# Demo 1: NonlinearSolve.jl (High-level, automatic)
# ==============================================================================

using NonlinearSolve
using Powerful.AutodiffInterface

residuals!, dae, sys_ws = make_residual_function(sys, Float64)

println("\n=== Demo 1: NonlinearSolve.jl ===")

# Option 1a: Automatic sparsity detection
prob = NonlinearProblem(
    NonlinearFunction(residuals!; sparsity=SymbolicsSparsityDetection()),
    copy(dae.y)
)
@time sol = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson(autodiff=AutoSparseForwardDiff()))
println("Converged: ", SciMLBase.successful_retcode(sol.retcode))
println("Residual norm: ", norm(sol.resid, Inf))

# Option 1b: Pre-declared sparsity (faster)
sparsity = jacobian_sparsity_pattern(sys)
println("Jacobian sparsity: $(nnz(sparsity)) / $(length(sparsity)) nonzeros")

prob = NonlinearProblem(
    NonlinearFunction(residuals!; jac_prototype=float.(sparsity)),
    copy(dae.y)
)
@time sol = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson(autodiff=AutoSparseForwardDiff()))

# ==============================================================================
# Demo 2: Manual Sparse Jacobian (Low-level, maximum control)
# ==============================================================================

println("\n=== Demo 2: Manual Sparse Jacobian ===")

using SparseDiffTools, ForwardDiff

# Setup (one-time cost)
sparsity = jacobian_sparsity_pattern(sys)
colors = matrix_colors(sparsity)
J = Float64.(sparsity)
g = similar(dae.y)

println("Matrix colors: ", maximum(colors), " (originally $(size(J, 2)) columns)")
println("Compression ratio: ", size(J, 2) / maximum(colors))

# Newton iteration
copyto!(dae.y, sol.u)  # Use solution as initial guess
max_iter = 20
tol = 1e-8

for iter in 1:max_iter
    # Compute Jacobian using coloring
    @time forwarddiff_color_jacobian!(J, residuals!, dae.y; colorvec=colors)

    # Compute residuals
    residuals!(g, dae.y)

    # Newton step
    Δy = J \\ g
    dae.y .-= Δy

    res_norm = norm(g, Inf)
    println("Iter $iter: ||g||∞ = $res_norm")

    if res_norm < tol
        println("Converged!")
        break
    end
end

# ==============================================================================
# Demo 3: Compare with NonlinearSolve workflow
# ==============================================================================

println("\n=== Demo 3: Integration with NonlinearSolve ===")

using NonlinearSolve

# Define problem with NonlinearSolve
prob = NonlinearProblem(residuals!, copy(dae.y))

@time result = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson())
println("Converged: ", SciMLBase.successful_retcode(result.retcode))
println("Residual norm: ", norm(result.resid, Inf))

Performance Comparison

Expected performance characteristics:

MethodSetup TimeIteration TimeMemoryBest For
Symbolic detectionHigh (seconds)MediumHighPrototyping
Pre-declared sparsityLow (ms)LowLowProduction
Dense JacobianNoneHighVery HighSmall systems (<100 vars)
Manual analyticalNoneLowestLowestUltimate performance

Phase 2: Optimize (Week 2-3)

Phase 3: GPU Support (Future)

  • [ ] Investigate Enzyme.jl for GPU autodiff
  • [ ] Add GPU-compatible Jacobian computation
  • [ ] Benchmark GPU autodiff vs manual GPU kernels

Key Insights

  1. Minimal changes needed: The wrapper approach requires NO changes to existing code
  2. Sparsity is critical: For large systems, exploit sparsity (100x speedup typical)
  3. Coloring is magic: Reduces N evaluations to ~5-20 for typical power systems
  4. Type stability helps: Current type-stable design makes autodiff efficient
  5. GPU tradeoff: GPU autodiff is immature; manual kernels likely faster for now

Questions for Discussion

  1. Should we add additional NonlinearSolve.jl solver backends?
  2. Do we need GPU autodiff support immediately, or is CPU Jacobian sufficient?
  3. Should we implement analytical Jacobian alongside autodiff for comparison?
  4. What tolerance/convergence criteria should be used for production?
